questions.q: The polynomial function defined by $p(x) = x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 12$ has $(x - 3)$ as one of its linear factors. What are all and only the zeros of $p$?
questions.explain: Because $(x - 3)$ is a factor, 3 is a zero. Dividing $p(x)$ by $(x - 3)$ using synthetic or polynomial division yields $x^2 + 4x + 4$. Setting this quotient equal to 0, we can factor it as $(x + 2)^2 = 0$, giving a double root at $x = -2$. Therefore, the distinct zeros are -2 and 3.
questions.subject: Mathematics
